story: In the late 1950s Fela Kuti left Lagos to study at the London School of Music. Back in Lagos he played a mix of highlife and jazz that did not sell. In 1969, on a trip to the United States, he met Sandra Smith, a singer and former Black Panther. She gave him the writings of Martin Luther King Jr., Angela Davis and, above all, Malcolm X. Kuti came to see that he had not been playing African music. He worked it out with drummer Tony Allen. The new music drew on highlife, fuji and jùjú. The name Afrobeat was meant partly to set it apart from the soul of James Brown. Kuti renamed his band Africa '70. It played a residency at his own club, the Afrika Shrine, from 1970 to 1975. Brian Eno and David Byrne carried its polyrhythms into Talking Heads' 1980 album Remain in Light. In the late 1990s and early 2000s Antibalas helped start an Afrobeat scene in Brooklyn. Kuti's sons Femi and Seun play it today.

sentences.quote: Both worked on [[Talking Heads]]' highly acclaimed 1980 album ''[[Remain in Light]]'', which brought polyrhythmic Afrobeat influences to Western music.

disagreements: Record began 1970; the article dates it earlier: 'Afrobeat evolved in [[Nigeria]] in the late 1960s by [[Fela Kuti]]' and infobox 'cultural_origins  = 1960s'. 1970 matches the Africa '70 / Afrika Shrine residency start. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeat?action=raw)

Record origin Lagos: the article does not say the Afrika Shrine was in Lagos, only that Kuti returned to Lagos earlier; the story says 'his own club' without a city. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeat?action=raw)

Record came_from lists highlife, funk, modjazz; the article also names fuji, jùjú and Yoruba music as sources ('Afrobeat was influenced by a combination of different genres, such as [[highlife]], [[Fuji music|fuji]], and [[Jùjú music|jùjú]]'). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeat?action=raw)
notes: Tree led_to nigerianreggae is not mentioned in the article and was not sourced. The article says the name was coined partly against James Brown; an external link says this happened in Accra (Ghana), not sourced here. Everything comes from one article; a second source (e.g. the Fela Kuti or Tony Allen articles) could add Tony Allen's drumming detail.
